newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FUND IPF KB SEES 1996 NET LOSS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FUND IPF KB SEES 1996 NET LOSS.

text.p: The Czech investment fund, IPF KB, said on Wednesday that preliminary results showed a net accounting loss of 1.937 billion crowns for the 1996 calendar year, and no dividend was expected to be paid.

"In October and November the fund conducted a ... re-evaluation of the portfolio, which ended in the result of an accounting loss," Ivan Lackovic, spokesman of fund manager IKS Komercni Banka, said in a statement.
Czech funds have been forced to re-value their portfolio to take account of the shares from the country's coupon privatisation programme which were originally entered in accounts at nominal value.
Lackovic said that the loss would be covered by reserves set aside for the re-valuation of the fund, which he said had assets of 2.5 billion crowns.
"For reasons of the realisation of the accounting loss, the fund will not pay a dividend for 1996," the statement said.
The funds shares rose on Wednesday four crowns to close at 724 on the Prague Stock Exchange.
